dedupe_keys.name: riverine hydrokinetic energy resource assessment and map for the continental united states epri 2012

description: This EPRI technical report is the national assessment and map of the riverine hydrokinetic energy resource of the United States, carried out for the U.S. Department of Energy by the Electric Power Research Institute with the University of Alaska Anchorage, the University of Alaska Fairbanks and the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. It derives theoretical power for 71,398 river segments with mean annual flow above 1,000 cubic feet per second in the 48 contiguous states from NHDPlus discharge and slope, excluding segments with hydroelectric dams, and adds Alaska from manually compiled head and flow data for its eleven largest rivers. The theoretical resource is 1,146 TWh per year in the contiguous states and 1,381 TWh per year including Alaska. A recovery factor, developed from 32 HEC-RAS scenarios that account for minimum velocity and depth, device packing, efficiency and back effects, turns the theoretical figure into a technically recoverable resource by segment and by hydrologic region. Access: an 80-page PDF on OSTI under DOI 10.2172/1092058, free to download; segment-level results appear as tables and maps in the report. Licence: none stated beyond the EPRI copyright and DOE disclaimer. Caveats: figures are resource estimates, not project designs, 69 percent of segments have a recovery factor of zero, and the data are from 2012. It suits siting screens, capacity planning and resource-based scenario inputs for renewable expansion studies.
